framing.lineOfInquiry: Arjun Jain (P00055) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE033
framing.alternate: Arjun Jain (P00055) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was elsewhere at the time (alibi)
alternateHypotheses.statement: Arjun Jain was somewhere else when the incident happened.
alternateHypotheses.label: Strong

evidence.text: Recorded at Sector 56 Residential, Gurugram, 302.9 km from the scene, 180 min before the incident — could not have reached the scene by road in that time

alternateHypotheses.test: Verify the alibi record independently (CCTV, witnesses or receipts at that place and time) and check whether the device could have been carried by someone else.

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Arjun Jain was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Strong

evidence.text: Apart from being named in the FIR, no independent record (location, communication, financial) links this person to the incident

alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Arjun Jain was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 41 other days (17 Apr – 13 Jun), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Arjun Jain's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: In contact with Ashok Thakur since 2025-04-17, 28 days before the incident (11 calls, 5 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Jasleen Thakur since 2025-04-17, 27 days before the incident (17 calls, 14 messages) — a long-standing relationship

comparison.verdict: The alibi alternate (A1) is currently better supported than the line of inquiry: records place Arjun Jain elsewhere and none place them at the scene.

note: Each hypothesis is tested from both sides to reduce confirmation bias. Confidence scores are evidential balance (not probability of guilt). Human review is required.
